Q1338879.label: Eric Williams
Q1338879.desc: first Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago (1911–1981)
Q1338879.summary: Eric Eustace Williams was a Trinidadian politician, who has been dubbed the "Father of the Nation" having led the then-British Colony of Trinidad and Tobago to majority rule on 28 October 1956, to independence on 31 August 1962, and republic status, on 1 August 1976, leading an unbroken string of general election victories with his political party, the People's National Movement, until his death in 1981. He represented Port of Spain South in the Parliament of Trinidad and Tobago.

Q51586047.label: Democrats
Q51586047.summary: The Democrats, known as Together – Civic Democracy from 2018 until 2023, and later the Blue Coalition, is a Slovak political party founded in 2018 by Miroslav Beblavý. The party has changed leadership multiple times and is led by the former Minister of Defense of Slovakia Jaroslav Naď since 2 December 2023.

Q134165503.label: 2025 Vancouver car attack
Q134165503.desc: attack at the Lapu Lapu Festival in Canada
Q134165503.summary: On April 26, 2025, a vehicle-ramming attack took place shortly after the Lapu-Lapu Day festival, a public celebration of Filipino heritage in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The attack left 11 people dead and at least 32 more injured, making it the deadliest attack in Vancouver's history.

Q215551.label: comparative advantage
Q215551.desc: in economics, the advantage one has over others in producing a particular good due to a lower relative marginal cost prior to trade
Q215551.img: مثال دافيد ريكاردو في الميزة النسبية.svg
Q215551.summary: Comparative advantage is an economic principle that explains why people, firms, and countries can often benefit from trade even when one party is more productive at producing every good or service. The principle states that greater gains from trade arise when each participant devotes a larger share of its labor and other productive resources to the activities with the lowest opportunity cost and obtains other goods and services through trade.

Q7209983.label: Polish Social Democratic Union
Q7209983.desc: social-democratic political party in Poland that existed from 1990 to 1992
Q7209983.summary: The Polish Social Democratic Union was a social-democratic political party in Poland that existed from 1989 to 1992. It was founded in 1989 under the name Social Democratic Union, under the leadership of Tadeusz Fiszbach with 25 parliamentary deputies, and changed its name in 1990. Along with the Social Democracy of the Republic of Poland, it is one of the successor parties of the Polish United Workers' Party (PZPR). The party itself was succeeded by the Labour Union.

Q178687.label: First Sino-Japanese War
Q178687.desc: 1894–1895 war between the Qing dynasty and the Empire of Japan over influence in Joseon, fought chiefly in Joseon
Q178687.summary: The First Sino-Japanese War was a conflict between the Qing dynasty of China and the Empire of Japan primarily for influence over Korea. In China it is commonly known as the Jiawu War. After roughly 7 months of sustained military gains by Japanese land and naval forces and the loss of the ports of Lüshunkou and Weihaiwei, the Qing government sued for peace in February 1895 and signed the Treaty of Shimonoseki two months later, ending the war.

Q9215.label: Sigmund Freud
Q9215.desc: Austrian psychiatrist and founder of psychoanalysis (1856–1939)
Q9215.summary: Sigmund Freud was an Austrian neurologist and the founder of psychoanalysis, a clinical method for evaluating and treating pathologies arising from conflicts in the psyche through dialogue between patient and psychoanalyst, and the distinctive theory of mind and human agency it posits.
